newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says too few elderly get pneumonia vaccinations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says too few elderly get pneumonia vaccinations.

text.p: A study of three different pneumonia outbreaks among elderly nursing home patients found evidence that fewer than five percent of them had obtained the recommended vaccine that could have protected them, federal health officials said Thursday.

The U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reviewed three nursing homes in Massachusetts, Oklahoma and Maryland where 36 cases of pneumonia occurred among a total of 267 residents. Nine of the patients died.
Known vaccination rates at the three nursing homes ranged from 1.9 percent to 4.5 percent, well below the national average for people 65 and older.
"We believe that certainly more than five percent of the residents may have been vaccinated, but without documentation, it's tough to say," the CDC's Dr. John Moroney said.
Researchers said pneumonia vaccinations are often overlooked in nursing homes. Doctors are sometimes hesistant to propose the vaccine if they lack individual patient records.

"If there's uncertainty about a patient's vaccination status with respect to the pneumococcal vaccine, we're recommending that physicians go ahead and possibly give a second dose rather than take the chance of leaving the patient unprotected," Moroney said.
